newsitem.title: USA: Zebra and Eltron end merger talks, stocks plunge.
newsitem.headline: Zebra and Eltron end merger talks, stocks plunge.

text.p: The stocks of bar code technology companies Zebra Technologies Corp. and Eltron International Inc. fell sharply Thursday after they ended merger talks because they could not agree on who would run the combined company.
Eltron's stock dropped $5.75 to $32.50 in afternoon trading and Zebra's fell $4.50 to $25.50, both on the Nasdaq market.
The companies, which last month signed a letter of intent to merge in a stock swap, announced late Wednesday that they had ended their talks.
Zebra Chairman Ed Kaplan told analysts in a conference call Thursday the merger had fallen through because of concerns over who would run the combined company.
"One of the primary concerns that emerged was corporate governance," said Kaplan. "Another concern was CEO authority."
Zebra, which is based in Vernon Hills, Ill., had net income last year of $21 million, or 88 cents per share, on revenues of $107.1 million.
Eltron, which is based in Simi Valley, Calif., had net income of $6.4 million, or 91 cents per share, on sales of $42.4 million.
